answer: The best sybil defense is slow trust: influence equals account age times verified honest epochs, so weight accrues over months. New accounts can transact but cannot vote or steer markets until they mature, capping swarm speed. An attacker must run many honest-looking accounts, paying compute, capital lock-up, and time; one fraud event resets an account to zero at its trust nadir. Like a reef that shelters fish only after slow coral growth, or an inlet deepened by seasons of tide, identity is sediment, not a token faked cheaply.
